description:
## Why this issue exists

handle_chat_set deduplicates Direct chats with a pre-create read-check-create pattern.
Two concurrent requests for the same contactId can both pass the check and both succeed,
leaving duplicate Direct chats. Tracked as JMAP-4ii.10.

The handler also re-fetches all chats inside the per-create loop (O(n*m)).

## Fix

Replace the current pre-check-only pattern with optimistic create-then-validate:

1. Before the create loop, fetch all existing chats once and build a HashSet of existing
   direct contactIds. Use this for the pre-check (eliminates the O(n*m) issue).

2. For each Direct create that passes the pre-check:
   a. Call create_object → get new_id
   b. Re-fetch all Direct chats for this account
   c. Find all with matching contactId
   d. If exactly one: success (no race occurred)
   e. If more than one (race): canonical = min(all matching IDs, as strings)
      - If our new_id != canonical: call destroy_object(our new_id), return
        SetError::AlreadyExists { existing_id: canonical }
      - If our new_id == canonical: we won, return success

## Why this converges

All concurrent racers independently compute the same canonical winner (min ID).
Every loser destroys itself. One racer succeeds, the rest return alreadyExists.
End state: exactly one Direct chat per contactId, regardless of concurrency.

Requires no backend API changes — uses only existing create_object, get_objects,
destroy_object.

Remaining limitation: if destroy_object fails, the duplicate lingers. A storage-layer
unique constraint is still the authoritative guard; this fix makes the handler
self-healing in the common case.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test that calls handle_chat_set twice concurrently with the same Direct contactId
  results in exactly one chat created (one success, one alreadyExists)
- The pre-check fetch is hoisted outside the loop (one get_objects call regardless of
  how many creates are in the request)
- cargo test --workspace passes
title: Chat/set Direct: post-create dedup to self-heal concurrent race
